patient_summary:
Hello you,

I understand you're feeling uncomfortable with your hands. You've been having dry, cracked hands that are very itchy and painful. You've been using a special soap to wash your hands, but it seems to be making your skin even more sore. You've been wearing gloves, but that hasn't helped much.

Today, we're going to try a new treatment. We'll use a cream called Aristocort, which we'll apply three times a day. We'll also use another cream called Polysporin, and we'll mix them together in equal parts. This will help your skin feel better.

We'll also tell you to stop using the soap and wash your hands with a gentle cleanser called Cetaphil. This cleanser might be a bit harsh on your skin, so we'll be careful with it.

We're also going to give you a medicine called Keflex. It's a special antibiotic that we'll give you 500 mg twice a day for two weeks. If you don't feel better after this, we'll see you again in one month. If you need it more often, we'll send a note to your doctor.

If you feel any pain or if your hands get worse, please call us right away. We're here to help you feel better.

Take care, you.
caregiver_checklist: Give Aristocort ointment 0.1% and equal part of Polysporin ointment three times a day (t.i.d.) and as needed (p.r.n.) for itch.
Check hands for dryness and cracking, and monitor for any new symptoms.
Watch for signs of infection such as increased redness, swelling, or pus.
Call if there is worsening of symptoms or new symptoms like fever.
Schedule a follow-up appointment in one month if not better, or on a as-needed (p.r.n.) basis.
Call if the pain or burning from Cetaphil cleansing lotion persists or worsens.
Schedule a refill for Keflex 500 mg twice a day (b.i.d.) for two weeks.
Watch for signs of allergic reaction to Keflex, such as rash or swelling.
Call if there are any signs of side effects from Claritin or Zyrtec, such as drowsiness or hives.

You've been washing them with soap, which made your skin hurt. You're going to talk to a doctor who will help you. They'll give you medicine to help your skin feel better. You'll use a special cream three times a day. You'll also take a medicine for a few days. The doctors and grown-ups are taking care of you.
source_text: SUBJECTIVE:,  This is a 29-year-old Vietnamese female, established patient of dermatology, last seen in our office on 07/13/04.  She comes in today as a referral from ABC, D.O. for a reevaluation of her hand eczema.  I have treated her with Aristocort cream, Cetaphil cream, increased moisturizing cream and lotion, and wash her hands in Cetaphil cleansing lotion.  She comes in today for reevaluation because she is flaring.  Her hands are very dry, they are cracked, she has been washing with soap.  She states that the Cetaphil cleansing lotion apparently is causing some burning and pain because of the fissures in her skin.  She has been wearing some gloves also apparently.  The patient is single.  She is unemployed.,FAMILY, SOCIAL, AND ALLERGY HISTORY: , The patient has asthma, sinus, hives, and history of psoriasis.  No known drug allergies.,MEDICATIONS: , The patient is a nonsmoker.  No bad sunburns or blood pressure problems in the past.,CURRENT MEDICATIONS:,  Claritin and Zyrtec p.r.n.,PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:,  The patient has very dry, cracked hands bilaterally.,IMPRESSION:,  Hand dermatitis.,TREATMENT:,1.  Discussed further treatment with the patient and her interpreter.,2.  Apply Aristocort ointment 0.1% and equal part of Polysporin ointment t.i.d. and p.r.n. itch.,3.  Discontinue hot soapy water and wash her hands with Cetaphil cleansing lotion.,4.  Keflex 500 mg b.i.d. times two weeks with one refill.  Return in one month if not better; otherwise, on a p.r.n. basis and send Dr. XYZ a letter on this office visit.
